svg.title: AGV and garage coordinate systems
svg.desc: Animated: the garage frame G (x east, y north), the heading measured from north counter-clockwise, the AGV body frame B (x forward along the long side, y left), locomote and strafe on two Pecos edges at W8, the planner's helper frame P (x out of the right side, y forward) and its neighbour-slot names, footprints built in P, a rotation-sign inconsistency at a hypothetical 45 degree heading, and a table of which source file uses which frame.
svg.metadata: ["The garage frame G: +x east, +y north, +z up (NodeAccuracy.msg). Every node position in the layout YAML is an (x, y) in metres in G: W8 is at (30.8823, 12.7753); the XL parking window of stall P5 is 5.791 m along x and 2.21 m along y. North is 'garage local north', a direction defined in the CAD file (GaragePose.msg).", "The heading theta. GaragePose.heading is an int16 in degrees, [-179, 180]; GeometricPose.yaw is the same angle in radians. It is measured from garage local north (+y), counter-clockwise positive: 0 faces north, 90 west, -90 east, 180 south. W8 lists headings [0, 90], so with the reciprocals its four poses face all four directions.", "The body frame B of AGV-1 at (8, 90): +x_B points along the long side in the heading direction (the locomote direction), +y_B to the left, +z_B up. In G the forward unit vector is f(theta) = (-sin theta, cos theta) and the left one (-cos theta, -sin theta); at theta = 90: west and south. B is the 'AGV frame' of NodeAccuracy.msg; its axes are the team's definition, the snapshots do not spell them out.", "Locomote = translation along body x, strafe = along body y. IsLocomoteOrStrafe (agv_motion_type.cpp) compares the edge bearing atan2(dy, dx) with heading + pi/2 (the math angle of +x_B) and with heading (the math angle of -y_B), each within 1e-3 rad or its reciprocal. W8 -> W31: bearing pi = 90 deg + pi/2, a LOCOMOTE of 2.857 m west. W8 -> W13: bearing pi/2 = heading, a STRAFE of 4.391 m north.", "The helper frame P that the planner's geometry code uses: B turned by -90 deg, so x_P points out of the AGV's right side (= -y_B) and y_P forward (= +x_B); p_G = p_node + R(theta) p_P, i.e. the heading used directly as a math angle. PoseGraph names its slots in P: FORWARD = +x_P = W13 (strafe right), BACK = W4 (strafe left), LEFT = +y_P = W31 (forward locomote), RIGHT = W9 (backward locomote).", "Footprints are built in P and then rotated by the heading. RectangleFromSize(width, length) puts its length argument along x, so AgvEntity's RectangleFromSize(kAgvLength, kAgvWidth) lays kAgvLength along y_P = +x_B, and a payload window's length_m also lies along y_P. Pecos check: at heading 90 the AGV's long axis and the XL window's 5.791 m lie along world x, the long side of stall P5.", "A sign inconsistency, read from the code and not observed. boost's rotate_transformer turns clockwise for positive angles. CreateRectangularPolygon and BayOdpEntity pass -heading (net counter-clockwise, correct); CollisionEntity::PolyAtPose passes +heading (net clockwise). At a hypothetical heading 45 the collision-table footprint of an AGV or payload would point north-east instead of north-west. At multiples of 90 deg, all Pecos uses, the centred rectangles coincide.", "The complete picture: one AGV, three frames. G for positions and headings, B for what the AGV does (locomote along x_B, strafe along y_B, NodeAccuracy offsets), P inside the planner's geometry and slot names. The table lists every source file that fixes one of them."]
